claim: Let \(k\) be a field of characteristic \(0\), let \(G\) be an abelian group, and let \(c:G\to(k,+)\) be a nonzero homomorphism. In the translation skew group ring \(A=k[X]\rtimes G\) with \(u_gX=(X-c(g))u_g\), put \(K=\ker c\) and \(C=kK\). Then \(Z(A)=C\), and contraction/extension gives a lattice isomorphism between all two-sided ideals of \(A\) and all ideals of \(C\): every two-sided ideal \(I\) satisfies \(I=A(I\cap C)\), while \(AJ\cap C=J\) for every ideal \(J\subseteq C\). Products satisfy \((AJ_1)(AJ_2)=A(J_1J_2)\), so prime and maximal two-sided ideals correspond exactly to prime and maximal ideals of \(C\). If \(G\cong\mathbb Z^d\) and \(r=\operatorname{rank}_{\mathbb Z}c(G)\), then \(C\cong k[z_1^{\pm1},\ldots,z_{d-r}^{\pm1}]\). The characteristic-zero hypothesis is sharp for this correspondence: in characteristic \(p\), for \(G=\mathbb Z\) and \(c(1)=1\), the invariant polynomial \(X^p-X\) produces a proper two-sided ideal whose intersection with \(k\ker c\) is zero.
integrity: The universal result is established by a direct symbolic proof. No finite computation is presented as evidence for an infinite statement, and the inaccessible-source risk is explicitly retained.
scientific_limitations: The contraction-extension theorem assumes an abelian acting group and characteristic zero. Positive characteristic admits extra translation-invariant polynomials, and a potentially relevant 2001 crossed-product paper could only be compared through its accessible abstract.
title: Ordinary ideals in translation skew group rings are controlled by the action kernel
